answer: Because the lotus hash is checked against the dawn checkpoint at intake, the canyon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 2 epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
